blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Difficulty is one of the most fundamental properties of a question: it determines whether the question can meaningfully discriminate between models of differing ability.
Although a variety of methods can now estimate or predict difficulty automatically, they yield only a single descriptive number, with no account of the underlying factors that make a question difficult in the first place.
In this work, we propose a data-driven approach that automatically generates and validates natural-language hypotheses explaining what makes one question harder than another.
We first estimate each item’s difficulty from the responses of a large pool of LLMs using Item Response Theory.
We then sample contrasting sets of easy and hard questions and prompt an LLM to propose candidate explanations of the difference, which are subsequently validated and selected on held-out questions. Experimental results across three datasets spanning mathematical, logical, and commonsense reasoning show that our method produces interpretable and predictive hypotheses.
On their own, they predict the difficulty of unseen questions competitively with, or better than, advanced black-box difficulty regressors; used as additional features, they further improve those regressors, implying that they discover difficulty signals that existing models fail to capture.
Moreover, we demonstrate that editing questions according to a hypothesis can shift their measured difficulty in the expected direction, indicating that the discovered hypotheses are causally valid difficulty factors rather than post-hoc descriptions.
Our approach thus turns a purely descriptive difficulty score into actionable statements.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The rapid growth of LLM capabilities has led to saturation on existing benchmarks ( Akhtar et al., 2026 ) , driving continuous benchmark iteration: harder, more challenging datasets are needed to keep discriminating between increasingly capable models ( Rein et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; White et al., 2025 ) .
Yet what determines the difficulty of a question in the first place remains poorly understood.
Prior work on question difficulty has largely focused on measuring difficulty and predicting difficulty.
Measurement typically relies on the responses of test-takers.
The representative approach in this field is the Item Response Theory (IRT) family of models ( Hambleton and Swaminathan, 2013 ; Hambleton et al., 1991 ) , which decomposes observed performance into item properties and test-taker ability.
IRT has increasingly been adopted for LLM evaluation ( Zouhar et al., 2025 ; Cui and Sachan, 2025 ) .
However, it only yields a descriptive number per item but does not reveal the underlying factors that make an item hard in the first place.
blocks.zh:
LLM能力的快速增长导致现有基准的饱和度(Akhtar等人,2026年),驱动着持续的基准迭代:需要更硬,更具有挑战性的数据集来继续区分能力不断增强的模型(Rein等人,2024年;Wang等人,2024年;White等人,2025年)。
然而,首先决定问题难度的是什么,人们仍然不了解。
以前关于问题难度的工作主要侧重于衡量难度和预测难度.
衡量通常取决于测试者的反应。
这一领域的代表性做法是模型反应理论(IRT)系列(Hambleton和Swaminathan,2013年;Hambleton等人,1991年),它将观测到的性能分解为项目属性和测试塔克能力。
在LLM评价中越来越多地采用IRT(Zouhar等人,2025年;Cui和Sachan,2025年)。
然而,它只得出每个项目的描述性数字,但并没有揭示使一个项目一开始就变得困难的根本原因。

blocks.en:
Some follow-up work ( Fischer, 1973 ; Janssen et al., 2004 ; Boeck and Wilson, 2004 ) attempted to represent an item’s difficulty as a linear combination of hand-specified item features, such as the cognitive operations it requires.
This turns difficulty from a free parameter into an outcome of question properties, and thereby shifts the question from measuring difficulty to predicting and explaining it.
A line of feature-based difficulty prediction followed across domains ( Benedetto et al., 2023 ; AlKhuzaey et al., 2024 ) .
Such features, however, must be designed by domain experts and coded by hand, which makes these approaches hard to scale across domains or to large question pools.
More recent work instead predicts difficulty with neural network or pre-trained LLMs that read the item difficulty directly ( Huang et al., 2017 ; Benedetto et al., 2020 ; Loginova et al., 2021 ) .
While these methods usually enjoy stronger performance and greater flexibility they predict difficulty from representations that are themselves uninterpretable, and therefore provide little insight into what makes a question difficult.
blocks.zh:
一些后续工作(Fischer,1973年;Janssen等人,2004年;Boeck和Wilson,2004年)试图代表一个项目作为手定项目特征的线性组合的难度,如它所需要的认知操作.
这使得难度从自由参数变为问题属性的结果,从而将问题从衡量难度转向预测和解释.
一系列基于地物的难度预测跟踪到各个域(Benedetto等人,2023年;Al Khuzaey等人,2024年)。
然而,这些特征必须由域专家设计,并用手进行编码,这使得这些方法难以跨越域或大问题库。
较近期的工作则预测了直接读取物品难度的神经网络或预训LLMs的难度(Huang等人,2017年;Benedetto等人,2020年;Loginova等人,2021年)。
虽然这些方法通常具有更强的业绩和更大的灵活性,但它们从本身无法解释的表述中预测出困难,因此对是什么使得问题变得困难,没有多少见解。

blocks.en:
On the other hand, a recent line of work uses LLMs to generate natural-language explanations for surface regularities in unstructured data ( Zhou et al., 2024 ; Zhong et al., 2022 ; Zhong et al., 2023 ; Zhong et al., 2024 ; Hollmann et al., 2023 ) .
These methods typically group data that are likely to share a property, and then prompt an LLM to describe a pattern the group has in common.
So far, these methods have mostly been applied to properties that are semantically explicit and directly observable in the text, for example, the topic, stance, or style (e.g., ”is about sports” , ”is written in the first person” ( Zhong et al., 2022 ) .
Such properties are relatively easy to discover.
In this work, we target difficulty , a property that is latent rather than annotated, continuous rather than categorical, and the product of many interacting factors, and that is correspondingly harder to explain.
We first estimate item difficulty with an IRT model from the responses of a large pool of LLMs.
We then repeatedly sample contrasting data of easy and hard questions and present them to an LLM to propose plausible explanations of the difference.
We explore various sampling strategies to make the discovery more effective, and validate and select the most informative hypotheses on a held-out set of questions 1 1 1 We defer a detailed discussion of related work to Appendix A . .
blocks.zh:
另一方面,最近的一行工作使用LLMs来生成非结构化数据中表面规律的自然语言解释(周等人,2024年;钟等人,2022年;钟等人,2023年;钟等人,2024年;霍尔曼等人,2023年).
这些方法通常将可能共享属性的数据分组,然后提示一个LLM来描述该组具有共同的模式.
迄今为止,这些方法大多适用于文本中明确和直接可见的属性,例如,专题、姿态或风格(例如,“关于运动”、“以第一人称书写”(Zhong等人,2022年))。
这种特性比较容易发现。
在这项工作中,我们针对的是困难,这种财产是潜在的而不是附加说明的,是连续的,而不是绝对的,是许多相互作用因素的产物,因此很难解释。
我们首先从一大批有限责任公司的答复中估算一个IRT模型的项目难度。
然后,我们反复抽样比较简单和困难问题的数据,并将这些数据提交给一个LLM,以提出对差异的合理解释。
我们探索各种抽样战略,使发现更加有效,并验证和选择关于一组搁置的问题的最为翔实的假设。

blocks.en:
We apply our approach to generate hypotheses for various benchmarks, including mathematical reasoning, logical deduction, and commonsense reasoning.
Experimental results show that our approach can generate higher-quality and valid explanations than other baseline generators.
Individually, our generated explanations separate difficulty more sharply than explanations from baseline approaches, and collectively they predict difficulty of unseen questions as well as or better than finetuned difficulty predictors and few-shot LLM judges.
Moreover, incorporating the generated explanations as features into these predictors further improves the performance, indicating that they capture difficulty-related information the existing models can not.
Finally, we use the hypotheses to curate synthetic questions: we edit questions so that they satisfy or violate a given hypothesis and observe that their measured difficulty shifts in the expected direction.
This demonstrates that the discovered hypotheses are not merely post-hoc descriptions but carry causal effect, which yields practical guidance for designing and iterating on benchmarks.
blocks.zh:
我们运用我们的方法来产生各种基准的假设,包括数学推理,逻辑推理和常识推理.
实验结果表明,我们的方法可以产生比其他基线发电机质量更高、有效的解释。
单独而言,我们产生的解释将困难比基线方法的解释更明显地区分开来,它们集体预测了隐形问题的困难,或者比微调的困难预测器和少见的LLM评断器更好。
此外,将生成的解释作为特征纳入这些预测器,进一步提高了性能,表明它们能捕捉现有模型无法获取的与难度有关的信息。
最后,我们用假说来解析合成问题:我们编辑问题,以便它们满足或违反某一假设,并观察到它们测量到的难度会向预期方向转移。
这表明,所发现的假说不仅仅是事后的描述,而是具有因果关系的,这为设计和延长基准提供了实际指导。

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
Our method consists of three steps.
First, we use IRT to estimate each question’s difficulty.
Second, we construct contrastive samples of hard and easy questions and prompt LLMs to generate candidate hypotheses explaining the difficulty gap.
Third, we refine and select from these candidate hypotheses.
The full pipeline is illustrated in Figure 1 .

首先,我们用IRT来估计每个问题的困难。
其次,我们构建了困难和简单问题的对比性样本,促使LLMs生成对困难差距的解释的候选假设.
第三,我们从这些候选假设中完善和选择。

blocks.en: 2.2 Hypothesis Generation

blocks.en:
Our core idea is to present LLMs with contrastive sets of difficult and easy items, and instruct an LLM to generate hypotheses explaining the difficulty gap between them.
We split the dataset into three disjoint sets: a generation set 𝒢 \mathcal{G} used to generate candidate hypotheses, a verification set 𝒱 \mathcal{V} to verify and select them, and a test set 𝒯 \mathcal{T} for the final evaluation.
Each set is constructed via difficulty-stratified sampling, ensuring coverage across the full difficulty range.
We repeat the sample–generate procedure for multiple rounds on 𝒢 \mathcal{G} to collect a sufficient pool of candidate hypotheses.

blocks.en: 3.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: 3.1 数据集

blocks.en:
We evaluate our method on three popular benchmarks across various tasks:
(1) GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) ( N = 1,319 N=1,319 ) is a widely used benchmark of grade-school math word problems that require multi-step arithmetic reasoning;
(2) BBH-structured ( N = 1,396 N=1,396 ) comprises six subtasks in the BBH dataset ( Suzgun et al., 2023 ) that require logical reasoning: ”logical deduction (three, five, and seven)” , ”reasoning about colored objects” , temporal sequences , and ”penguins in a table” ;
(3) Winogrande ( Sakaguchi et al., 2021 ) ( N = 1,267 N=1,267 ) is a dataset to test commonsense reasoning with pronoun resolution problems while minimizing the surface-level statistical biases present in the original Winograd Schema Challenge ( Levesque et al., 2012 ) .
The difficulty of this dataset is known to be difficult to predict ( Ding et al., 2024 ) .
We use it as a challenging testbed to test the limit of baselines and our method.
We collect LLM response records from RouterEval ( Huang et al., 2025 ) , including 5,000 LLMs for GSM8K and WinoGrande, and 3,811 LLMs for BBH-structured.
We fit a 1PL IRT model implemented in py-irt ( Lalor and Rodriguez, 2023 ) , which estimates the model by stochastic variational inference.

We evaluate the quality of the generated hypotheses along two dimensions: • Predictive effect – to what extent do they explain and predict the difficulty of unseen questions?

We report the adjusted R 2 R^{2} ( Ezekiel, 1930 ) , which corrects for the upward bias of R 2 R^{2} as the number of predictors grows, to measure the goodness of fit of the hypotheses as features and their explanatory power.

blocks.en: 3.3 Baselines
blocks.zh: 3.3 基线

blocks.en: NLParam ( Zhong et al., 2024 ) learns natural-language predicates as model parameters by optimizing a continuous relaxation of each predicate in embedding space and then prompting an LLM to verbalize it, iteratively replacing the least useful predicate. We use its classification variant with the logistic layer replaced by linear regression on IRT difficulty.
blocks.zh: NLParam(Zhong等人,2024年)通过在嵌入空间中优化每个上游的持续放松,然后促使一个LLM对它进行语言化,迭代取代最不有用的上游,从而将自然语言的上游学作为模型参数. 我们使用它的分类变体,后勤层被ITT困难的线性回归所取代。

blocks.en:
HypotheSAEs ( Movva et al., 2025 ) applies SAEs to turn the embeddings into sparse interpretable features which are then are selected via Lasso and verbalized into a hypothesis.
We obtain embeddings from the hidden-state activations of Gemma-3-4B ; because the evaluation set we use is not sufficient to finetune an SAE, we use the pretrained SAEs from Gemma-Scope-2, and have an LLM ( Gemini-3.7-Flash ) refine the verbal description of each selected feature using the questions from our dataset on which it activates.
blocks.zh:
假想SAEs(Movva等人,2025年)应用SAEs将嵌入物转化为稀疏的可解释特征,然后通过拉索选择,口头化为假说.
我们从Gemma-3-4B的隐藏状态激活中获取嵌入;由于我们所用的评价集不足以微调一个SAE,所以我们使用Gemma-Scope-2的预先训练的SAE,并且有一个LLM(双子座-3.7-Flash),利用我们数据集中它激活的问题来完善对每个选定特性的口头描述.

blocks.en: HypoGeniC ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) generates hypotheses from labeled examples with an LLM and improves them iteratively using a bandit-style reward. As HypoGeniC is defined for classification, we adapt it to difficulty by discretizing IRT difficulty into 3 buckets and treating level prediction as the classification task.
blocks.zh: HypoGeniC(Zhou et al., 2024)从标有LLM的示例中生成假说,并使用匪类风格的奖励进行反复改进. 由于HypoGeniC的定义是用于分类的,我们通过将IRT的难度磁盘化成3桶,并将水平预测作为分类任务来适应难度.

blocks.en: Edisa ( Hua et al., 2023 ) is a slice detection model that discovers coherent groups of error-prone examples by fitting a mixture Gaussian model using embedding, label, and error distance. We adapt it to our setting by replacing the error distance of a single model with the IRT difficulty, and by verbalizing each discovered slice with an LLM prompted with its representative members. We set the number of slices to the hypothesis budget ℋ \mathcal{H} , and use the same embeddings as for Qwen3-Embedding-4B .
blocks.zh: Edisa(Hua等人,2023年)是一种切片检测模型,它利用嵌入、标签和误差距离,安装一种混合物高斯模型,从而发现一致的易发生错误的例子群。 我们通过用IRT困难取代单一模型的误差,用代表成员所激发的LLM对每一个发现的片段进行口头描述,来适应我们的设定。 我们设定了假设预算 H\ mathcal{H} 的切数, 并使用与 Qune3- Embedding-4B 相同的嵌入符 。

blocks.zh: 4. 假设评价

blocks.en: 4.1 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.1 主要成果

blocks.en:
We present top hypotheses generated by our method in Table 1 .
Every hypothesis is plausible and interpretable. Most of them concern the cognitive demands that the corresponding task actually imposes on the solver—the operations that have to be carried out and the information that has to be held and manipulated—rather than surface features of the text such as question length.
On GSM8K, our method also captures issues of data quality: items whose reference answer is itself flawed, which affect only a small fraction of the data but carry a very large difficulty effect.
In terms of the statistical measures, the 95 % 95\% CI of SEP {\rm SEP} has a lower bound above zero for 13/15 hypotheses, showing that they genuinely discriminate between hard and easy items.
Except on Winogrande, whose difficulty is known to be hard to perceive even for humans ( Ding et al., 2024 ) , 9/10 hypotheses on the two other datasets reach at least a medium effect † , and half of them reach a large effect ‡ .

我们在表1中提出了由我们的方法产生的最高假设。
每一个假设都是可信的和可解释的。 其中大多数涉及相应的任务实际上对解决者提出的认知要求,即必须进行的操作以及必须持有和操纵的信息,而不是像问题长度这样的文本的表面特征。
在GSM8K上,我们的方法还捕捉到数据质量的问题:其参考答案本身有缺陷的项目,这只影响到一小部分数据,但具有非常大的难度效应.
在统计计量方面,公共教育部95%的95%CI对13/15的假设有低于零的界限,表明它们真正地区分硬项目和易项目。
除了在Winogrande上,人们知道即使对人类也很难察觉到它的难度(Ding等人,2024年),另外两个数据集的9/10假设至少达到中效 ,一半达到大效 .

blocks.en:
We fit an OLS regression of item difficulty using the generated hypotheses as features on the test set, and report adjusted R 2 R^{2} as a goodness-of-fit measure of their explanatory power (i.e., the in-sample setting in § 3.2 ).
The results are present in Figure 2 , where our method achieves the best fit at most hypothesis budgets on three datasets.
More importantly, the baselines saturate quickly: they yield only 5–10 effective hypotheses, beyond which adjusted R 2 R^{2} declines, indicating that the additional hypotheses carry noise rather than real signal.
Our method, in contrast, keeps producing informative hypotheses.
We attribute this to the fact that the baselines generate patterns directly from the data and therefore discover only the most salient signals, whereas our sampling strategy allows the model to explore new difficulty factors by repeatedly contrasting difficult and easy questions.
blocks.zh:
我们用生成的假说作为测试集的特征来匹配项目难度的OLS回归,并报告经调整的R 2 R^{2}作为对其解释力(即第3.2节中的模拟设置)的适切度量。
图2显示了结果,其中我们的方法在三个数据集的假设预算中最多能取得最佳效果。
更重要的是,基线饱和速度很快:它们只产生5–10个有效的假说,超过这些假说调整了R 2 R^{2}的下降,表明附加假说带有噪音而不是真实信号.
与此相反,我们的方法不断产生内容丰富的假设。
我们将此归因于以下事实:基线直接从数据中产生规律,因此只发现最显著的信号,而我们的取样策略则允许模型通过反复对比困难和容易的问题来探索新的困难因素.

blocks.en:
We now examine how well ℋ \mathcal{H} predicts the difficulty of unseen questions.
We train an OLS regressor on 𝒢 \mathcal{G} and 𝒱 \mathcal{V} using the hypotheses as features and evaluate its R 2 R^{2} on the test set, comparing our method against the baseline difficulty predictors introduced in § 3.3 .
The results are presented in Table 2 .
Overall, our model achieves the best performance on two datasets, GSM8K and WinoGrande, and the second best on BBH-structured, showing that these features alone already constitute a strong difficulty predictor.
We note that all models perform poorly on WinoGrande.
This again echoes the finding that the difficulty of WinoGrande is hard to predict ( Ding et al., 2024 ) 3 3 3 On Winogrande, human annotators agree with the IRT-estimated difficulty on only 73.4 % 73.4\% of item pairs. Under a bivariate-normal assumption, this agreement level implies R 2 ≈ 0.45 R^{2}\approx 0.45 as a ceiling. .
Nevertheless, our method still extracts some signal on this dataset, while all baselines except Claude-Sonnet-5 fail completely, attaining R 2 R^{2} values around or even below 0 0 .

blocks.en:
So far we have compared our hypothesis-based difficulty predictor against strong baselines.
In practice, however, our method is complementary to them rather than competing with them: the hypotheses it discovers can be supplied to existing predictors as additional features.
We test this on three semantic predictors–fine-tuned RoBERTa-base , Gemma-3-4B and Qwen3-Embedding-4B —by adding each method’s hypothesis match vector as a second feature block.
Figure 3 reports the gain in test R 2 R^{2} .
Our hypotheses give the largest gain of any hypothesis source in all settings.
The gains are largest on GSM8K: + 0.19 +0.19 and + 0.18 +0.18 over the two frozen embeddings, and + 0.11 +0.11 even over the fine-tuned RoBERTa ( 0.362 → 0.468 0.362\rightarrow 0.468 ), by far the strongest baseline there.
On BBH-structured the gain over the strongest model is small: RoBERTa-base already reaches R 2 = 0.646 R^{2}=0.646 there, and our hypotheses add only + 0.008 +0.008 on top of it (they still add + 0.05 +0.05 to the two frozen embeddings), implying that on this dataset the difficulty signal is largely already captured by the encoder itself.
On WinoGrande, all baselines sit at around 0 0 , yet our hypotheses lift each of them to R 2 R^{2} between 0.08 0.08 and 0.10 0.10 .

Figure 5 compares three prompting strategies: group-only, pair-only, and a mixture of group and pair prompts.
The first two are designed to discover hypotheses at different granularities.
For the mixture, we keep the total number of questions fixed and vary the proportion of group versus pair prompts for fair comparison, with the range of results across these proportions shown in the shaded region.
On GSM8K, group-only converges faster, although pair-only reaches comparable or better performance with a larger budget.
On BBH, the two perform similarly.
On both datasets, however, interpolating between them under the same budget yields better results in most cases (shadow area), scales better as the budget grows, and reaches a higher upper bound (orange line).
This suggests that mixing the two strategies indeed discovers complementary hypotheses.

Figure 5 compares the effect of contrast strength: sampling high-contrast questions (bucket gap δ ≥ 7 \delta\geq 7 ; Eq. 2 ), sampling low-contrast questions ( 4 ≤ δ ≤ 6 4\leq\delta\leq 6 ), and mixing the two.
The former is designed to capture more pronounced difficulty patterns, while the latter more nuanced signals.
The two strategies behave in opposite ways on the two datasets: high contrast is the stronger choice on GSM8K, while low contrast wins on BBH-structured.
The mixed strategy serves as a more stable option: it does not beat the better single strategy at every budget, but it stays close to it in most cases.

We test whether a hypothesis captures a difficulty-bearing property through targeted question editing (see examples in Table 3 ).
Because the difficulty signal in WinoGrande is inherently weak, we focus here on GSM8K and BBH-structured.
We randomly sample 50 test questions, determine which hypotheses apply to each of them, and prompt an LLM to edit and verify the questions, changing only what the hypothesis describes while leaving the rest intact. Details are given in Appendix C.5 .

blocks.en:
We evaluate the causal effect using the difficulty shift and the success rate defined in § 3.2 .
Measuring the difficulty of an edited question would require re-evaluating it on thousands of LLMs, which is prohibitively costly.
We therefore re-run only a subset of LLMs, chosen to cover a range of performance levels (from below 10% to above 80% accuracy) and limited to models under 30B due to the restriction of our compute resource.
A reliable difficulty re-estimation is not attainable from this subset, so throughout this section we use accuracy as a proxy for difficulty 4 4 4 Under the 1PL model an item’s mean accuracy over a fixed respondent set is a strictly monotone function of its difficulty, so the direction of a within-panel accuracy change matches the direction of the difficulty shift. .
Because each hypothesis applies to a different set of questions (those it can meaningfully rewrite), and induces a different kind of edit, comparing hypotheses against one another in a controlled, fair setting is difficult, which in turn makes a comparison against the baselines difficult.
In this section we therefore focus on validating the effectiveness of our own hypotheses.
blocks.zh:
我们利用第3.2节界定的难度变化和成功率来评估因果关系。
要衡量一个经编辑的问题的困难,就必须对数千个有限责任公司重新加以评估,费用高昂。
因此,我们只重新运行一个子集的LLM,由于我们计算资源的限制,被选择涵盖一系列性能水平(从10%以下到80%以上),并且仅限于30B以下的模型.
在这个子集中无法实现一个可靠的困难再估计,因此在整个这一节中,我们用精确度作为困难4 4 4的代名词,在1PL模型中,一个物品相对于固定的应答集的平均值准确度是其困难的严格单调函数,因此一个小组内部精度变化的方向与难度转移的方向一致. 。 。 。
因为每个假说都适用于不同的一组问题(那些可以有意义地改写的问题),并诱导不同的编辑类型,在受控,公平的环境下将假说相互比较是困难的,这反过来又使得与基线比较变得困难.
因此,在本节中,我们侧重于验证我们自己的假设的有效性。

In Table 4 we report the difficulty shift and success rate averaged over all hypotheses, which shows consistent bidirectional changes on both datasets.
Increase-difficulty edits reduce mean accuracy by 15.27 and 23.88 percentage points on GSM8K and BBH-structured, respectively, while decrease-difficulty edits improve it by 32.18 and 28.52 points.
Question-level alignment reaches 70.9% and 92.2% for increase and decrease edits on GSM8K, compared with 77.6% and 85.5% on BBH-structured.
Thus, the aggregate changes are accompanied by directional consistency across most edited questions, rather than only a few large shifts.

因此,在总体变化的同时,大多数经编辑的问题都具有方向一致性,而不只是几个大转变。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we presented a hypothesis generation method for explaining what makes a question difficult.
Rather than treating difficulty as a number to be estimated, we take it as a quantity to be explained: we measure difficulty with IRT from the responses of thousands of LLMs, sample contrasting sets of easy and hard questions, and prompt an LLM to propose natural-language hypotheses.
Experiments on three datasets show that the resulting hypotheses are interpretable and of high quality. They capture difficulty signals that semantic encoders do not, predict the difficulty of unseen questions as well as or better than black-box predictors, and further improve those predictors when added as features. Beyond prediction, they also guide the editing of questions to manipulate their difficulty in a controlled direction, which suggests that they identify genuine sources of difficulty rather than post-hoc correlations. We hope this offers a step toward benchmarks whose difficulty can be understood and designed, rather than only measured.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们提出了一个假设生成方法来解释是什么使得问题变得困难.
我们不把困难当作一个可以估计的数字,而是把它当作一个需要解释的数量:我们从数千个LLM的回复中衡量IRT的困难,样本对比了几组简单而难的问题,促使LLM提出自然语言的假设.
对三个数据集的实验显示,由此产生的假设是可解释的,质量很高. 它们捕捉到语义编码器没有的难度信号,预测隐形问题的难度以及或者比黑盒预测器更好,并在添加为特性时进一步改进这些预测器. 除了预测外,它们还指导对问题的编辑,以操纵它们在一个控制方向上的难度,这表明它们识别出真正的难度来源而不是后热相关. 我们希望,这为实现各项基准迈出了一步,这些基准的困难是可以理解和设计的,而不仅仅是可以衡量的。

blocks.en: Appendix A Related Work
blocks.zh: 附录A 相关工作

blocks.en:
Difficulty Modeling. Question difficulty is a central quantity wherever questions are used to measure ability.
In educational testing it determines which items enter an exam, how scores are compared across test forms, and which item an adaptive test presents next ( Van der Linden et al., 2000 ) ; it also has to be known for newly written questions before they can be administered, which has motivated predicting and controlling the difficulty of generated items ( Cui and Sachan, 2023 ; Jiao et al., 2023 ) .
In LLM evaluation it has become equally consequential: benchmarks are filtered or rebuilt around the items that remain hard ( Kipnis et al., 2025 ; Zouhar et al., 2025 ) , and item-level difficulty is used to pick informative subsets, to test models adaptively at a fraction of the cost ( Hofmann et al., 2025 ; Polo et al., 2024 ) , or to weight items when ranking models by competency ( Hu et al., 2026 ) .
How difficulty is obtained falls into two families.
They first estimates it from responses: descriptive IRT models treat each item’s difficulty as a free parameter, while explanatory item response models constrain it to be a function of item covariates, classically a linear combination of the cognitive operations an item requires ( Fischer, 1973 ; Janssen et al., 2004 ) .
These covariates are specified by experts, so the explanation is only as complete as the expert’s list; our approach can be seen as an explanatory model whose covariates are discovered from data.
The second family predicts difficulty from the item text alone.
Early work relied on hand-designed linguistic and cognitive features ( Benedetto et al., 2023 ; AlKhuzaey et al., 2024 ) , which were then replaced by neural encoders of the item ( Huang et al., 2017 ; Loginova et al., 2021 ) , the approach that dominated the recent shared task on medical exam items ( Yaneva et al., 2024 ) ; Byrd and Srivastava (2022) extend this line beyond difficulty to discrimination, relating both parameters to textual and contextual properties of the question.
With the arrival of LLMs, difficulty has been estimated by prompting them to judge items against IRT-derived levels, by scoring the plausibility of the candidate answers ( Mozafari et al., 2026 ) , and by reading it off the hidden states of the answering model itself ( Lugoloobi and Russell, 2025 ) .
Closest to our goal, Dutulescu et al. (2024) use LLMs to analyze which features are associated with question difficulty; there the features are drawn from a predefined inventory and examined post hoc, whereas we let the model propose candidate explanations, validate each of them on held-out items, and select among them by their joint predictive power.
blocks.zh:
难以建模。 凡用问题衡量能力,问题难度就是一个核心数量。
在教育测试中,它决定了哪些项目进入考试,如何在考试表格中比较分数,以及下一个是哪一个适应性测试(Van der Linden等人,2000年);它还必须以新的书面问题而闻名才能管理,这促使人们预测和控制生成项目的难度(Cui和Sachan,2023年;Jiao等人,2023年)。
在LLM评价中,它也产生了同样的后果:基准被过滤或围绕仍然坚硬的项目重建(Kipnis等人,2025年;Zouhar等人,2025年),项目层次的困难被用来挑选信息子集,以成本的一小部分对模型进行适应性测试(Hofmann等人,2025年;Polo等人,2024年),或者在按能力对模型进行排名时对项目进行加权(Hu等人,2026年)。
如何获得困难取决于两个家庭。
他们首先从答复中作出估计:描述性IRT模型将每个项目的困难视为自由参数,而解释性项目响应模型则限制它成为项目共变的一个函数,在经典中是项目所需的认知操作的线性组合(Fischer,1973年;Janssen等人,2004年)。
这些共变物由专家指定,因此解释只与专家名单一样完整;我们的方法可以看作是一个解释模型,从数据中发现了共变物.
第二家族只从项目文本中预测困难.
早期的工作依赖于手设计的语言和认知特征(Benedetto等人,2023年;Al Khuzaey等人,2024年),后来被物品的神经编码器所取代(Huang等人,2017年;Loginova等人,2021年),这种方法主导了最近共同承担的体检项目的任务(Yaneva等人,2024年);Byrd和Srivastava(2022年)将这条线延伸至超越了歧视的难度,同时涉及到问题的文字和背景属性.
随着LLMs的到来,通过促使他们对照IRT衍生的水平判断项目,通过评分候选人答案的可信度(Mozafari等人,2026年),并通过从答案模型本身的隐藏状态(Lugolobi和Russell,2025年)读出来,来估计难度.
与我们的目标最接近的是,Dutulescu等人(2024年)使用LLMs分析哪些特征与问题难度相关;其中的特征取自预先确定的清单并经过事后审查,而我们则让模型提出候选解释,在被搁置的项目上验证每个特征,并根据其联合预测力加以选择。

blocks.en:
Automated Error Analysis. A related area, slice discovery, seeks to discover the data on which an AI model is prone to err and to explain the patterns behind those errors, which is in essence also a form of explanation of difficulty.
Early work assumed structured inputs and searched over conjunctions of feature values for slices on which a model performs significantly worse than average, with the slice definition itself serving as the explanation ( Chung et al., 2019 ; Sagadeeva and Boehm, 2021 ) ;
Later methods instead look for coherent, underperforming regions of a model’s representation space and attach natural-language descriptions to the regions they find, by matching them to captions in a shared embedding space or by prompting an LLM with their members ( d’Eon et al., 2022 ; Eyuboglu et al., 2022 ; Hua et al., 2023 ) .
What these methods explain, however, is the difficulty an item poses to one particular model.
The errors of a single model, however, are likely to confound the difficulty of an item with the weaknesses and biases of that particular model, rather than reflecting an intrinsic property of the item.
While effective for model debugging, the weaknesses these methods uncover are therefore unlikely to transfer to other models, and offer limited insight into the broader questions of how a dataset should be curated and iterated on.
blocks.zh:
自动错误分析. 一个相关的领域,即切片发现,寻求发现AI模型容易出错的数据,并解释这些错误背后的规律,这实质上也是解释困难的一种形式.
早期工作假定了结构化输入,并对一个模型表现比平均值差得多的切片的特征值组合进行搜索,将切片定义本身作为解释(Chung等人,2019年;Sagadeeva和Boehm,2021年);
后来的方法是寻找一个模型的表示空间的连贯、表现不佳的区域,并将自然语言描述附在其发现的区域,方法是将它们与共用嵌入空间中的标题相匹配,或与其成员一起推动LLM(d ' Eon等人,2022年;Eyuboglu等人,2022年;Hua等人,2023年)。
然而,这些方法解释了一个项目给某一特定模式造成的困难。
然而,单一模式的错误可能使某一项目的难度与该特定模式的弱点和偏差相混淆,而不是反映该项目的内在属性。
虽然这些方法对模型调试有效,但发现的弱点不可能转移到其他模型,对数据集应如何整理和重现的更广泛问题提供有限见解。

blocks.en:
Hypothesis Generation with LLMs. A growing line of work uses LLMs to describe, in natural language, the patterns shared by a group of data.
These methods first partition the data into groups that are likely to share a pattern or behavior, for example, by taking samples with different labels or from different corpora ( Zhong et al., 2022 ; Zhong et al., 2023 ) , or by clustering or otherwise exploiting structure in embedding space ( Zhong et al., 2024 ; Movva et al., 2025 ) .
They then prompt an LLM with samples from these groups to generate descriptions of what the samples have in common, typically followed by some form of validation of the generated descriptions.
Across previous approaches, the property being explained is usually one that is observable in the text or supplied as a label: a topic, stance, or writing style, the aspects that drive a product rating, membership of a given group, or an annotated outcome such as engagement or persuasiveness ( Zhong et al., 2022 ) . Our work keeps the propose-and-verify structure of this line but changes the target and the evaluation: the property is a latent, continuous quantity inferred from model responses rather than annotated, the contrasting groups are constructed by sampling from that quantity, and hypotheses are scored by how much of its variance they explain, individually and jointly, on items never used for their discovery.

The method presumes a classification target, so we discretize difficulty into three equal-frequency levels and map a predicted level back to that level’s mean difficulty when regression metrics are needed.
Apart from these adaptations, we follow the original implementations as closely as possible.
10 initial items seed ten initial hypotheses.
A bank of 20 hypotheses is then maintained by an upper-confidence-bound rule with exploration weight 0.5 0.5 , the 10 highest-scoring hypotheses vote on each new item, and a pool of ten mispredicted items triggers a generation of five new hypotheses whose rewards are initialized on the most recently scored items.
We also ran a stricter variant in which generation only ever sees the generation pool 𝒢 \mathcal{G} and rewards only ever come from the validation pool 𝒯 \mathcal{T} .
We stop generation once the model has seen a fixed number of questions, matching the number seen by our method, as a proxy for the budget to ensure a fair comparison.

blocks.en:
We construct hypothesis-guided question edits in three stages.
First, we determine whether the original question
satisfies the target hypothesis using its binary match label.
If the property is present, we request its removal or simplification.
If it is absent, an applicability judge assesses whether it can be
introduced naturally while preserving the question’s broad setting
and answer format; inapplicable interventions are skipped. Second, a rewriter produces a separate candidate for each applicable
intervention (including questions and reference answers), targeting the specified property while preserving the
question’s broad setting and answer format.
Third, Gemini and Astra verify the candidates in sequence, each
solving the rewritten question from scratch and checking its
solvability, intended property change, and preservation of the
original setting. Malformed or incomplete responses are retried, and
only rewrites accepted by both verifiers enter the evaluation.
